issues.reason: `LocatedIn` is stated to be "containment ONLY — in / at / inside / within", and the place-inside-a-place rule carves out exactly this case ("a relational noun that states a link rather than a position — a tributary OF the larger river — is the ordinary genitive"), so reading the of-phrase as containment asserts a position the text does not state.

new_gaps: The genitive one-test ("is the possessed a part / component of the possessor?") is undecidable for a mass constituent of a geographic feature — the water of a cove is arguably neither a component in the "car engine" sense nor a possession (it is closer to what the cove consists of), and `PartOf` is elsewhere barred from geography, so nothing states which head carries the link.
defect_summary: The link takes the ordinary genitive of *Possessive / genitive NP* — `(PartOf sk_water_1 sunken_cove)` if the water counts as a component of the cove, otherwise the opaque `(Possession sk_water_1 sunken_cove)` — never `(LocatedIn …)`; which of those two is the licensed head for a mass constituent of a geographic feature is itself unstated and filed as a gap.
notes: Name handling matches the Kestrel River pattern exactly (one opaque symbol, its Name atom, the kind atom from the name-internal head, no modifier genus), and the bare-plural generic rule at 0.9/0.9 with `Agent` for the self-moving subject and `Source` for "from" is right.
